name: Omaha
description: Omaha is a community-card poker variant where each player receives four hole cards and must use exactly two of them with exactly three of the five board cards to make their best five-card hand. The constraint makes hand-reading and drawing significantly different from Texas Hold'em.
alsoKnownAs: Omaha Hi-Lo Eight or Better Poker

overview.description: Omaha is a community-card poker variant where each player receives four hole cards and must use exactly two of them with exactly three of the five board cards to make their best five-card hand. The constraint makes hand-reading and drawing significantly different from Texas Hold'em.

history.origins: Omaha emerged in the 1980s, likely in casino card rooms, and rapidly became a staple of both live and online poker. It derives from Texas Hold'em but adds the mandatory two-from-hand, three-from-board rule.
timeline: 1980s: First documented in American casino circles.
1990s: Spread to European poker rooms and tournaments.
2000s: Pot Limit Omaha (PLO) becomes the dominant variant online.
Present: Second only to Hold'em in tournament and cash-game popularity.
history.cultural: Known as 'the game of the nuts' because hand values run closer; draws and redraws are frequent.
history.evolution: Omaha High-Low 8-or-Better (Omaha/8) split the pot between best high and best qualifying low hand, adding strategic depth.

setup.dealing: Each player receives four hole cards face-down. Five community cards are dealt in stages: flop (3), turn (1), river (1).
setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips, dealer button.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best five-card hand at showdown, using exactly two hole cards and exactly three board cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. Blinds posted (small and big blind). 2. Each player receives four hole cards. 3. First betting round (pre-flop). 4. Dealer burns one card and deals three community cards (flop). 5. Second betting round. 6. Burn and deal one card (turn). 7. Third betting round. 8. Burn and deal one card (river). 9. Final betting round. 10. Showdown: each active player must use exactly two hole cards and exactly three board cards to make their best hand.
keyRules: Exactly two hole cards and exactly three board cards must be usedâ€”no more, no fewer.
Pot Limit Omaha (PLO): maximum raise equals current pot size.
Omaha/8: Pot splits 50/50 between best high hand and best qualifying low (8-or-better); ace plays low for low.

strategy.basic: Play hands with coordinated cardsâ€”same suits and close ranks for straights and flushes. Four random high cards are weaker than 9-10-J-Q double-suited.
strategy.intermediate: Blockers matter: if you hold two Aces, opponents are less likely to have nut flush draws. Fold marginal hands pre-flop; Omaha punishes loose play.
strategy.advanced: Equity runs close; avoid overvaluing top set on a coordinated board. Nut draws (e.g. nut flush + straight draw) have strong implied odds.
tips: Position is crucialâ€”late position lets you see more action before committing.
In Omaha/8, scooping (winning both halves) is the key to profit; avoid playing hands that can only win one way.

variations.name: Omaha High
variations.description: Standard pot-limit or fixed-limit; only the best high hand wins.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Same engine as base Omaha; overrides can be added later for limit or hand-size.

variations.name: Omaha Hi-Low 8-or-Better
variations.description: Pot splits between best high and best qualifying low (8-high or better). Commonly fixed-limit.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Same engine with high-low split; overrides for low qualifier can be added later.

variations.name: Five Card Omaha (Big O)
variations.description: Each player receives five hole cards; must still use exactly two with three board cards.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant differs by initialHandSize and finalHandSize; overrides to be added.

variations.name: Six Card Omaha
variations.description: Six hole cards; must use exactly two with three board cards.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant differs by hand size; overrides for six hole cards to be added.

variations.name: Courchevel
variations.description: One board card is dealt face-up before the first betting round; popular in France.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds pre-flop board card; overrides for deal pattern to be added.

scoring.description: Pot-split poker. No points; chips go to the winner(s). In Omaha/8, the pot is split between high and low.
scoring.winCondition: Best five-card hand wins the pot (or half in Omaha/8).

synthesis.shortDescription: Community-card poker where you get four hole cards but must use exactly two with three board cards. Pot Limit Omaha is the dominant variant.

hero.title: OMAHA
hero.subtitle: Four Cards, Two Choices
hero.tagline: Twice the cards, twice the decisions.
